AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How wet should a compost heap be? (1 mark)
   A. Dripping wet
   B. Covered by a pool of water
   C. Damp like a squeezed sponge
   D. Completely dry

2. Where should the holes in the pipe be placed? (1 mark)
   A. Next to each plant
   B. Only at the end of the row
   C. Far away from the plants
   D. Only near the bucket

3. Which is a benefit of drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Water is wasted
   B. Fewer weeds grow between plants
   C. The leaves get very wet
   D. More weeds grow

4. Which of these is a part of a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A container for water
   B. A scarecrow
   C. A tractor
   D. A compost heap

5. Which of these is a way of collecting water for the garden? (1 mark)
   A. Burning the roof
   B. Cutting down trees
   C. Collecting rainwater from a roof
   D. Digging up rivers

6. What is a good first step if a person's clothes catch fire? (1 mark)
   A. Run fast
   B. Wave the arms
   C. Stop, drop and roll on the ground
   D. Jump in the air

7. Where is a scarecrow best placed? (1 mark)
   A. Far from the crop
   B. Inside the house
   C. In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from
   D. At the river

8. Which of these is a small wild animal that can destroy crops? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Weaver bird
   C. Cow
   D. Hen

9. What is a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. A type of crop
   B. The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   C. A bed for sleeping
   D. A tool for digging

10. About how far apart may rows of tiny seeds be? (1 mark)
   A. 1 mm
   B. 10 metres
   C. 5 metres
   D. 15 to 20 cm

11. Why do we cover the seeds with a thin layer of fine soil? (1 mark)
   A. To stop them growing
   B. To let birds find them
   C. To protect them and keep them moist
   D. To make them bigger

12. What is thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Adding more seeds
   B. Making soil thin
   C. Cutting all plants
   D. Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room

13. Which of these is a climbing fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Guava
   B. Orange
   C. Mango
   D. Passion fruit

14. At what depth should the seedling be planted? (1 mark)
   A. The same depth as it was in the bag
   B. Upside down
   C. On top of the ground
   D. Very deep

15. Which of these fruits grows on a woody tree? (1 mark)
   A. Passion fruit
   B. Grapes
   C. Blackberry
   D. Mango

16. Which of these is a climbing fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Mango
   B. Orange
   C. Grapes
   D. Guava

17. Which is a pest problem for ripe fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Fruit flies and birds
   B. Sun
   C. Sand
   D. Stones

18. What should be done with extra fruits? (1 mark)
   A. Share or sell them and avoid wasting
   B. Throw them away
   C. Bury them
   D. Leave them to rot

19. Which of these is a sign of a healthy young fruit plant? (1 mark)
   A. Green leaves and steady growth
   B. Yellow and dry leaves
   C. Fallen stem
   D. Rotten stem

20. Why should a poultry house be clean and dry? (1 mark)
   A. To stop hens from laying
   B. To keep birds healthy and safe
   C. To attract rats
   D. To make eggs blue

21. Which meal is missing body-building foods? (1 mark)
   A. Ugali and sukuma wiki only
   B. Ugali, fish and spinach
   C. Chapati, egg and tomato
   D. Rice, beans and cabbage

22. What do body-building foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Help the body to grow and repair
   B. Make food taste sweet
   C. Only give heat
   D. Only quench thirst

23. Which way should you open a lid on a hot pot? (1 mark)
   A. Straight toward your face
   B. Away from your face
   C. Fast and close
   D. Under water

24. How can you tell that water is boiling? (1 mark)
   A. Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off
   B. The water is still
   C. The water is blue
   D. The water is cold

25. Why should the frying pan be heated before adding food? (1 mark)
   A. So that food browns and does not soak up oil
   B. To burn it
   C. To melt it
   D. To break it

26. Why should vegetables be boiled for a short time only? (1 mark)
   A. Long boiling makes them colder
   B. It saves nothing
   C. Short boiling makes them poisonous
   D. Long boiling destroys some vitamins

27. What should be placed under a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A basin or a soak pit
   B. A bed
   C. A plant only
   D. A radio

28. Why is a tippy tap useful? (1 mark)
   A. It needs electricity
   B. It works without a water tap and saves water
   C. It cleans clothes
   D. It makes soap

29. When should you wash your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Before eating and after using the toilet
   B. Never
   C. Only on Sunday
   D. Only after school ends

30. How can you make drinking water safe? (1 mark)
   A. Add soil
   B. Leave it in the sun uncovered
   C. Boil it and let it cool covered
   D. Stir it with a stick

31. Which is a method of cleaning the home? (1 mark)
   A. Planting
   B. Grafting
   C. Sowing
   D. Mopping

32. How can a dustpan be improvised? (1 mark)
   A. Use a sack
   B. Use a chair
   C. Use a rope
   D. Cut a jerrican or flat tin

33. Why should rubber boots not be dried in very strong heat? (1 mark)
   A. They become cleaner
   B. They get heavier
   C. The rubber can crack
   D. They grow

34. How should gumboots be dried? (1 mark)
   A. Upside down in a shady, airy place
   B. Under a heavy weight
   C. In a closed cupboard while wet
   D. Beside a hot fire

35. Why is a display of clean PPE useful? (1 mark)
   A. It makes PPE dirty
   B. It hides the PPE
   C. It helps others learn about PPE and hygiene
   D. It wastes time

36. Why should torn gloves not be used? (1 mark)
   A. They are too big
   B. They may not protect the hands
   C. They are too heavy
   D. They are too clean

37. What is the use of a scarecrow shirt made with tacking? (1 mark)
   A. It is eaten
   B. It waters plants
   C. It is a tool
   D. It clothes the scarecrow using stitches

38. What should you do at the end of a sewing lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Count the needles and pins
   B. Leave them
   C. Throw them
   D. Hide them

39. Which skill from Mathematics helps in tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Measuring
   B. Naming shapes only
   C. Adding money
   D. Telling time

40. When is long and short tacking a good choice? (1 mark)
   A. For long straight seams where a quick hold is enough
   B. It is never used
   C. For curves only
   D. For hems on very slippery cloth

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three reasons why PPE should be cleaned. (3 marks)

42. Give three ways of caring for a fruit crop. (3 marks)

43. Plan a group project of making a scarecrow shirt using tacking. Give materials, steps, safety and how the group shares work. (5 marks)

44. Give two reasons why we should not kill wild animals that eat crops. (2 marks)

45. A school wants to make compost from kitchen and garden wastes. Write a plan with the materials, the place, the steps and the safety measures. (5 marks)

46. Design a hygiene log for one week. List five practices to record and explain how you will use it. (5 marks)

47. Describe how to boil eggs. (4 marks)

48. Give three benefits of using compost manure on the farm. (3 marks)

49. State the difference between boiling and shallow frying. (2 marks)

50. Describe how to keep a food journal for one week. (4 marks)

51. Plan a class display of cleaned PPE. Say what you would show and what information cards you would write. (5 marks)

52. Describe how a family can plant trees to help conserve fuel. (4 marks)

53. Prepare a balanced menu for one day for a Grade 4 child using local foods and explain why it is balanced. (5 marks)

54. Give three signs that fruit is ripe, naming the fruit. (3 marks)

55. A family boils beans for a long time on a big fire with the lid off. Suggest five ways to improve fuel use. (5 marks)

56. Give two advantages of boiling food. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Damp like a squeezed sponge
   Too dry stops rotting and too wet makes the heap smell sour.

2. A — Next to each plant
   Water must fall near the roots.

3. B — Fewer weeds grow between plants
   The soil between plants stays dry so fewer weeds grow.

4. A — A container for water
   A container holds water for the pipe or bottle.

5. C — Collecting rainwater from a roof
   Rainwater tanks store water for dry days.

6. C — Stop, drop and roll on the ground
   Rolling smothers the flames.

7. C — In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from
   It must be seen by the animals that come to the crop.

8. B — Weaver bird
   Weaver birds and other birds eat grain crops.

9. B — The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   A seedbed is where seeds are sown.

10. D — 15 to 20 cm
   Rows are close but leave space for weeding.

11. C — To protect them and keep them moist
   Covering helps seeds germinate.

12. D — Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room
   Thinning gives strong plants space.

13. D — Passion fruit
   Passion fruit needs support to climb.

14. A — The same depth as it was in the bag
   Planting too deep can rot the stem.

15. D — Mango
   Mango grows on a woody tree.

16. C — Grapes
   Grapes grow on vines.

17. A — Fruit flies and birds
   Ripe fruit attracts flies and birds.

18. A — Share or sell them and avoid wasting
   Extra fruits can earn money or feed others.

19. A — Green leaves and steady growth
   Healthy plants grow green.

20. B — To keep birds healthy and safe
   Dirty houses spread diseases.

21. A — Ugali and sukuma wiki only
   Ugali and kale give energy and vitamins but no protein food.

22. A — Help the body to grow and repair
   They are rich in protein.

23. B — Away from your face
   Steam can burn.

24. A — Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off
   These are signs of boiling.

25. A — So that food browns and does not soak up oil
   Food placed in cold oil soaks up oil.

26. D — Long boiling destroys some vitamins
   Vitamins are lost with too much cooking.

27. A — A basin or a soak pit
   To catch the dirty water.

28. B — It works without a water tap and saves water
   It can be made from a jerrican.

29. A — Before eating and after using the toilet
   These are key times.

30. C — Boil it and let it cool covered
   Boiling kills germs.

31. D — Mopping
   Mopping cleans floors.

32. D — Cut a jerrican or flat tin
   A cut jerrican forms a scoop.

33. C — The rubber can crack
   Heat damages rubber.

34. A — Upside down in a shady, airy place
   This drains water and protects the rubber.

35. C — It helps others learn about PPE and hygiene
   Displays teach and encourage others.

36. B — They may not protect the hands
   Holes let dirt and germs in.

37. D — It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   Tacking holds the shirt pieces together.

38. A — Count the needles and pins
   Counting ensures none is lost.

39. A — Measuring
   Measuring gives even and accurate stitches.

40. A — For long straight seams where a quick hold is enough
   It is quicker.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can carry germs, it may smell or spoil, and clean PPE lasts longer and protects better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watering, weeding, mulching, adding compost, pruning, protecting from animals (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: old cloth, needles, thread, scissors, chalk, ruler. Steps: measure and cut two pieces; pin; tack along sides; leave openings; sew firmly; stuff. Safety: count needles. Group: share tools, assign jobs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark materials, 2 marks steps, 1 mark safety, 1 mark teamwork.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: They are part of nature and biodiversity, and they help in other ways such as pollinating and eating pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: peelings, leaves, grass. Place: shaded, well-drained, near the garden. Steps: sticks, layers, water, cover, turn. Safety: gloves, wash hands, keep children away from the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 for place, 2 for steps, 1 for safety.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Practices: washed hands before meals, brushed teeth twice, bathed, clean clothes, drank safe water. Tick each day, count ticks at the end, and improve the practice with fewest ticks.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for practices and table, 2 marks for use.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, boil gently for about 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds crops, it softens the soil and helps it to hold water, and it is cheap because it uses waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct benefit.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boiling cooks food in bubbling water. Shallow frying cooks food in a thin layer of hot oil in a pan.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw a table; write what you eat at every meal; write the group of each food; at the end of the week check which groups were missing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Display gloves, gumboots, mask, headgear, overall, canvas shoes; cards say what each protects and how to clean it; safe storage; explain to visitors.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for items, 2 marks for cards, 1 mark for explaining.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant fast growing trees on their land for firewood, care for them and replace any tree cut with more new trees, so wood is always available and forests are not cut.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for planting, caring, replacing and result.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Breakfast: porridge and egg; lunch: ugali, beans and sukuma wiki; supper: rice, fish and cabbage with fruit. It includes energy, body-building and protective foods in every day.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for a menu with all groups, 2 marks for correct explanation.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Passion fruit turns purple or yellow and wrinkles; guava turns yellowish and smells sweet; pawpaw turns yellow or orange and gives when pressed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with fruit.

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: Soak the beans first, cook with the lid on, use dry wood, reduce the flame after boiling starts, cut food or use an improved jiko, put out the fire after cooking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: It needs no oil and it makes hard food soft and safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.
